I would keep my land split between the wheat-maize rotation and potato. I farm only 10.1 mu, and my family has off-farm work, so I would not make the plan too complicated. I would put 6.0 mu into the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest grain income for me under well irrigation, and I know that system well after many years. I would use the remaining 4.1 mu for potato, because it gives me cash income and spreads risk away from only relying on grain. For wheat, I would stay with improved seed, keep fertilizer moderate but solid, irrigate at the key stages, and aim for a stable yield instead of pushing too hard. For summer maize, I would use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen a little higher than wheat, and rely on quick planting after wheat harvest so I do not lose heat or moisture. For potato, I would use improved seed tubers, put more potassium into it than I do for wheat, and manage water carefully because potato responds well but is easy to damage if I get too aggressive. Overall, I would choose a practical plan that fits my land, my labor, my irrigation, and my habit of going for stable output rather than gambling on very high input.
